qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Massive client switching costs in institutional custody, fund administration, and middle-office processing, combined with multi-generational trust relationships in private wealth management. Proof of moat shown by 19.6% 5-year median ROIC and $5.0B in sticky servicing fees. Primary erosion threats stem from back-office automation by fintech challengers, scale advantages and pricing pressure from larger custody peers (BNY, State Street), and heavy regulatory capital requirements.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). While Northern Trust boasts an enduring, high-trust institutional custody and private wealth franchise with high switching costs (19.6% median ROIC), it operates as a deposit-funded custody bank with $153B+ in assets on $12.7B in equity (>12x balance sheet leverage) and $118B+ in deposits. In accordance with the Munger solvency standard, fractional-reserve and deposit-funded custody balance sheets fail Gate 6 due to inherent duration, interest-rate, and deposit flight vulnerabilities.
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 consolidated revenue of $8.09B with $5.02B in trust and servicing fees ($2.80B Asset Servicing, $2.22B Wealth Management) and $2.41B in net interest income. Total assets of $153.5B supported by $118.7B in deposits against $12.7B in equity, reflecting 12.1x leverage. 10-year median ROIC of 19.57% and owner EPS compounding from $4.51 (2016) to $12.70 (2025). Peak OE EPS was $13.11 in 2024. Despite high returns on tangible capital and deep fiduciary moat, the deposit-funded balance sheet is disqualified under Gate 6 criteria.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
